raw:
I remember the last shift I worked with a coworker who was retiring from the bookstore. I keep track of stock there, but what stays with me isn’t the work so much as the little signs that she was leaving. There was a farewell card beside the till, and I remember her name tag unpinned from her apron.

That made me sad. I knew she was retiring, of course, but seeing the name tag off her apron made it feel more final. I kept thinking about how she wouldn’t be there on another shift. I could be glad for her and still feel sorry that our time working together was ending.
